title: Beer Cost-Per-Pint vs Store-Bought
dataSources: Fermentation gravity/temperature (`brew:fermentation`), kegerator pours (`kegerator:pour`), wine-cellar climate (`winecellar:reading`).
app: Fermentation sensors (Tilt/iSpindel hydrometer, temperature), kegerator flow meters and scales, and wine-cellar climate sensors via MQTT and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=kegerator:pour
| stats sum(volume_ml) as poured_ml, sum(batch_cost) as cost by batch
| eval pints=poured_ml/473, cost_per_pint=round(cost/pints,2)
| sort cost_per_pint
description: Works out what each homebrewed pint actually costs once ingredients are spread across the batch, versus buying it.
value: Homebrew feels cheap until you count the ingredients; a real cost-per-pint tells you whether the hobby also saves money.
implementation: Record batch costs and pour volumes; schedule per batch and compare cost per pint to shop prices.
visualization: Bar chart of cost per pint by batch with a store-price reference.
grandmaExplanation: It works out how much each homemade pint really costs compared to buying beer from the shop.
